'''Robert House's double''' is a man who served as the body double of the real [[Robert House]] before the [[Great War]]. He appears in both [[Fallout TV series season 1|season 1]] and [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Background==
This man has been a close confidant of RobCo Industries founder [[Robert Edwin House]] since approximately [[Timeline#2067|2067]]. Similar-looking and similarly-dressed to the real Robert House, he is used by the real House for all public appearances, such as radio and television appearances, and to broadcast his thoughts to the general public, while maintaining anonymity and freedom of research. This man's image has become so closely associated with the real House that when Robert House himself appears in public, he is not widely recognized as the famous tycoon.<ref>{{FOTV|2|1}}</ref>

==In the TV series==
===Season 1===
====[[The Beginning]]====
{{Quotation|There's a lot of earning potential with the end of the world.|Mr. House double at a Vault-Tec meeting}}
Mr. House's double attends a meeting hosted by [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] executive [[Barb Howard]] at the [[Vault-Tec headquarters (TV series)|Vault-Tec headquarters]] in [[Los Angeles]] in 2077 as a representative of RobCo, along with [[Leon Von Felden]] on behalf of [[West Tek]], [[Julia Masters]] on behalf of [[REPCONN Aerospace]], and [[Frederick Sinclair]] on behalf of [[Big MT]].

During the meeting, House predicts Sinclair's failure in casino management and doubts the entire premise of Vault-Tec's plan, citing the idea that "rats" locked away for long periods will eventually "eat" each other. After Barb Howard of Vault-Tec reveals the idea of the Vault experiment and asks those present for ideas, House is the only one present who does not offer his own idea, although he does note that the plan has great potential for profit at the end of the world. He notes that Vault-Tec's plan requires significant investment but is based solely on hypothetical assumptions, and then asks for a guarantee that the Vaults would be useful. Barb proposes that the company can make good on its claims by directly initiating the nuclear war.

At this point in the series, the Robert House present at the meeting being a body double is not yet revealed. The episode presents itself as if he is the real Robert House, maintaining the secrecy surrounding the twist. In reality, the real Robert House was eavesdropping on the meetings from somewhere else, while the body double physically attended.

===Season 2===
====[[The Innovator]]====
The Mr. House double appears on television as the face of RobCo during an interview about anti-RobCo sentiment, where he proclaims that RobCo's goal is to optimize the workplace and that if the government needs help with international affairs, "they know who to call." [[Bill (TV series)|Bill]], a disgruntled protester, calls House a parasite and that no one voted for him, but he is interrupted by a stranger (the real Mr. House) who speaks highly of House's performance, claiming that he has more power than any politician in [[Washington, D.C.]] and agreeing with Bill's caustic comment that he is House's biggest fan. The stranger begins to rant about obsolescence, but Bill and his friends kick him out of the bar, threatening to beat him up.

Later, a radio news host announces that the Mr. House double stated that the question around nuclear war is not when the war would start, but who it will be initiated by.

====[[The Wrangler]]====
While Cooper Howard is walking around the Lucky 38 casino, the Mr. House double descends from the upper floors, whom Cooper mistakes for the real one. "House" approaches Cooper point-blank, accompanied by a bodyguard, and says Mr. House wants to see him. Having reached the building's penthouse, the fake House and Howard are met by [[Victor (Securitron)|Victor the Securitron]], who introduces Cooper to the real Robert House, sitting on a chair next to a large terminal. Cooper is surprised, as he had previously seen this man in the restroom at an [[American Veteran Entertainment Alliance]] awards ceremony. House reveals that he knows about Cooper's intent on assassinating him, and the Mr. House double reveals that he has been playing the role of Mr. House for over 10 years, calling it his career.

====[[The Other Player]]====
In a flashback from before his attendance of Vault-Tec's nuclear war meeting, Mr. House's double is seen meeting with Barb Howard in a conference room in the Vault-Tec headquarters, with [[Hank MacLean]] present to take notes. House's double presents RobCo's "Automated Man" technology -- the [[brain-computer interface chip]] -- to a confused Barb but a very interested Hank. Barb tries to refuse, saying that House already has control over multiple Vaults as part of a special arrangement with Vault-Tec, but House's double clarifies that this is a separate deal: he is giving this technology to Vault-Tec in exchange for being given the [[Cold fusion|cold fusion diode]], which he will use for his own "special project" in Las Vegas. When Barb asks him what this project is, House's double simply states that it is above her pay grade. 

==Notes==
Like the real Mr. House, the Mr. House double smokes cigarettes.

==Behind the scenes==
* Rafi Silver's character was not explicitly revealed to be a body double of Mr. House until "[[The Wrangler]];" in the two episodes where his character previously appeared, he was credited as "Robert House" himself. The actual Robert House (played by [[Justin Theroux]]) is left unnamed in the credits, though "The Wrangler" (as well as promotional materials for the second season of the TV series) confirmed that his character was the actual Robert House.
* The presence of a double for Mr. House is a reference to [[wikipedia:Howard Hughes|Howard Hughes]], a real-life historical figure who was one of the original inspirations behind Robert House. According to legend, Hughes used body doubles due to his extreme paranoia and even allegedly faked his own death in 1976. 
** In an interview from December 2025, [[Geneva Robertson-Dworet]] and Justin Theroux alluded to the relationship between Theroux's House and Silver's House body double, though they did not state it outright. Robertson-Dworet commented that this was based on Howard Hughes' increasing reclusiveness near the end of his life, stating that the writers wanted to depict House as someone "constantly playing tricks on the world, and was maybe somewhat scared to go out because, think of what a targeted man he is." Theroux suggested that House could have "become so paranoid, or so rarefied, that he needs to live above Las Vegas in a very protected place," also noting that the setting of the late 2070s made it "still possible to have avatars in the world where people wouldn't recognize [House]."<ref name="SR" group="Meta">[https://archive.ph/g9WiA Screen Rant: "Fallout Season 2: Justin Theroux On Taking Over Iconic Mr. House Role" (archived)]</ref>
* The theme of Robert House doppelgangers has been touched upon in official Fallout sources before: the "Prophet of Profit" plot hook for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]'' featured a man claiming to be Mr. House.
* Rafi Silver said that in preparation for his role as Mr. House's double, he watched numerous ''Fallout'' lore videos on YouTube, including ones by JuiceHead, MrMattyPlays, Oxhorn, and KnightRaven.<ref group="Meta">[https://www.youtube.com/shorts/kosGH9l-_vQ IGN: "Fallout's Mr. House really did his research" (YouTube Short)]</ref>
